name: Income / Covered-Call
tagline: Get paid now, give up the rip — these funds sell call options to convert future upside into a high monthly paycheck. Great in flat/down markets, they lag a plain index fund in bull runs.
universe_note: A fast-growing group. The big split is ACTIVE + ELN funds (JEPI, JEPQ) vs SYSTEMATIC 100%-overwrite funds (QYLD, XYLD) vs TACTICAL partial-overwrite (DIVO). New entrants launch often — use 'Add ticker' to pull any fund not listed here.
key_tensions: Yield is NOT return: a 10-12% distribution after capped upside often trails a plain S&P fund over multi-year bull runs. JEPI ~9.8%/yr since 2020 vs S&P ~13.2%.
Upside cap is the core cost: QYLD/XYLD write calls on ~100% of the portfolio (almost no upside); JEPI/JEPQ keep some; DIVO covers only part (keeps the most upside, yields least).
Return-of-capital / NAV erosion: QYLD's price fell from $25 (2013) to ~$18 while paying ~12% — part of the 'income' is your own principal handed back. JEPI/JEPQ/DIVO income is higher quality.
Active+ELN (JEPI/JEPQ) adds bank counterparty risk & opacity; systematic (QYLD) is transparent but rigid with max upside sacrifice; DIVO is active, writes options directly, tactically.
Tax: ELN income is ordinary income; index options (QYLD/XYLD) get 60/40 treatment; ROC defers tax but erodes basis. Best held in tax-advantaged accounts.
Short volatility: yields rise when markets are fearful (high VIX) and shrink in calm markets — the paycheck is variable, not contractual.
benchmark_note: SPY (plain S&P 500) is the yardstick, NOT an income fund. It keeps 100% of market upside at ~0.09% fee and ~1% yield. Compare each fund's TOTAL RETURN (not its yield) to SPY to see the true cost of the coupon — in 2024 SPY +24.9% vs JEPI +12.6%.

purity.note: Textbook equity-premium-income; distributions are mostly real premium + dividends, minimal return-of-capital.

etfs.overall: The blue-chip, lowest-drama covered-call ETF — diversified defensive sleeve, reliable ~8% income, lags a plain S&P fund in bull years.

memo.thesis: JEPI pairs a defensively built ~130-stock S&P sleeve with an options-income overlay, aiming to deliver most of the equity return with ~2/3 the volatility and a high monthly payout. It's the institutional-grade choice for equity income without QYLD-style NAV decay — best in tax-advantaged accounts.
memo.strategy: Owns ~130 low-beta stocks (its alpha source), then buys equity-linked notes (ELNs) whose payoff equals selling ~1-month, slightly out-of-the-money S&P 500 index calls. Collects premium (paid monthly) but forfeits index gains above the strike each month — so it captures only PARTIAL upside in a fast rally. The defensive stock picks cushion drawdowns. Softer upside cap than QYLD because strikes are OTM on the index.

purity_verdict.text: A clean equity-premium-income fund. Income is predominantly true option premium + dividends, not return of capital — the high-quality end of this theme.

memo.thesis: JEPQ applies JPMorgan's equity-premium-income engine to the Nasdaq-100, generating ~12% yield because tech options carry richer premiums. It delivered strong income AND total return through the 2023-25 tech bull, but carries materially more concentration and downside risk than JEPI.

etfs.name: Global X NASDAQ 100 Covered Call ETF

performance.note: Total return. PRICE fell from $25 (2013) to ~$18 — ~28% NAV erosion despite ~12%/yr payouts. A large, swinging share of distributions has been RETURN OF CAPITAL.

cost.note: 0.60% — pricey for a rules-based fund (25bps more than JPM's active funds).

purity.note: The purest, most literal covered-call mechanic — 100% at-the-money overwrite.

track_record.note: 12-yr record shows real NAV/price erosion + total return badly lagging QQQ despite the high payout.

etfs.overall: The original high-yield (~12%) systematic covered-call fund — maximum income, maximum upside sacrifice, and a long-term NAV decline that makes the 'yield' partly your own capital.

memo.thesis: QYLD maximizes current income by systematically writing at-the-money calls on its ENTIRE Nasdaq-100 portfolio, delivering a consistent ~12% headline yield. The trade-off is severe: it surrenders essentially all upside above the strike, so over a tech bull its price and NAV erode while QQQ compounds. Suitable only if you explicitly prioritize current cash flow over growth.
memo.strategy: Owns the Nasdaq-100 and each month sells AT-THE-MONEY index calls on ~100% of assets. ATM strikes maximize premium but mean almost no participation in monthly gains — if the Nasdaq jumps 8%, QYLD keeps roughly only the ~1-2% premium, not the rally. In down months it still falls (cushioned only by premium). The asymmetric profile structurally erodes NAV in rising markets.

purity_verdict.text: Most literal covered-call fund — but this 'purity' (100% ATM overwrite) is exactly what causes the NAV drag and return-of-capital.

etfs.name: Amplify CWP Enhanced Dividend Income ETF
etfs.derivatives: Yes — tactical direct calls on part of book

performance.note: Total return. Best upside capture of the covered-call funds (covers only part of the book). 30-day SEC yield ~1.6% EXCLUDES option premium — not return of capital.

cost.note: 0.56% — mid-pack (cheaper than QYLD, pricier than JEPI).

purity.note: More a dividend-equity fund with an OPPORTUNISTIC option overlay than a pure covered-call play.

concentration.note: Only ~20-25 core stocks; top-10 ~50% — real single-stock risk.

track_record.note: 9+ yrs, 5-star Morningstar; clean income (minimal ROC), strong risk-adjusted returns.

etfs.overall: The 'total-return-friendly' income fund — a concentrated blue-chip dividend portfolio with light, tactical call-writing; lower yield (~4.7%) but much better upside capture than QYLD.

memo.thesis: DIVO blends a hand-picked portfolio of ~20-25 blue-chip dividend payers with TACTICAL (not blanket) covered-call writing, targeting ~5% income plus capital appreciation. Because it covers only part of the book opportunistically, it keeps far more upside than full-overwrite funds — at the cost of a lower yield. The best 'total-return + income' compromise here, but concentrated.
memo.strategy: Holds a focused set of quality dividend stocks for dividends + appreciation, then tactically sells calls on INDIVIDUAL names when a stock shows strength or elevated implied volatility — rather than mechanically covering everything. Most of the portfolio stays uncapped most of the time, so DIVO participates in more of a rally than QYLD/JEPI (analysts estimate it gives up only ~30% of big up-months vs near-100% for QYLD). The trade-off: less premium, hence the lower ~4.7% yield. Writes options DIRECTLY (not ELNs).

purity_verdict.text: More a dividend-growth fund with an income overlay than a pure covered-call vehicle — a feature for total return, a caveat for 'covered-call purity'.

memo.concentration: The most concentrated fund here — ~20-25 stocks, top-10 ~50%; meaningful single-stock risk.
memo.sector_geo: US large-cap blue chips, diversified across financials/industrials/tech/consumer; 100% US.
memo.cost_context: 0.56% is mid-pack — cheaper than QYLD/XYLD (0.60%), pricier than JEPI/JEPQ (0.35%).
memo.track_record_note: 9+ yr record, 5-star Morningstar (Derivative Income). Yield quality is high and clean — the ~4.7% distribution is funded by real dividends + option premium with minimal ROC. The low ~1.6% 30-day SEC yield is NOT a red flag — SEC yield simply doesn't count option income. Total returns (16-17% in 2024-25) strong for an income fund.

⚠️ Still caps ~30% of strong up-months despite 'tactical' framing.

decision_log.text: Best blend of income + growth, but concentrated. If you want income without giving up most upside, this is the pick; accept the ~20-25 stock concentration and lower headline yield.
